LESSON: READING 10.4.1 PLAY: PROJECT

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How does an acted play differ from a written one?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify simple props and costumes that create mood and atmosphere

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify simple props and costumes that create mood and atmosphere
   In simple words: practise until you can identify simple props and costumes that create mood and atmosphere. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project.
4. Show that you can: identify simple props and costumes that create mood and atmosphere

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Dramatise simple scenes for classmates while focusing on voice, gestures and movements,
2. Discuss how to use role play and mime in the performance,
3. Self efficacy: It is enhanced as the learner performs in front of an audience.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does an acted play differ from a written one?
2. What makes a performance successful?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify simple props and costumes that create mood and atmosphere

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
